transcript:
Meeting Header: Date: 2026-12-28, Start 16:00 UTC, Approx duration 75 minutes, Format: All-hands / leadership update. Attendees: Maya (CEO), Ravi (VP Eng), Elena (VP Product), Ben (VP Sales), Priya (CFO), Lucas (Head Reliability), plus company-wide.

Summary: Quick year-end review, product roadmap recap (Redwood Optimize, Dedicated scale), ops & reliability update, SOC two progress, hiring and budget signals, Q1 priorities, open Q&A, recap + next steps.

[00:00:00] Maya: okay uh good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, I know it's, it's the tail end of year, appreciate you carving out the hour plus. we'll keep this tight but, uh, there's a few things we want to share before folks go on break. first quick wins: team shipped the Optimize pilot and the ded- dedicated autoscaling improvements, incredible work. big thank you to eng and product.

[00:01:12] Ravi: yeah I just, quick from eng, we've been running the new batching and KV cache changes in staging for three weeks, seeing about a 23% reduction in p99 token latency on the common workloads, and cost per token down roughly 15% after quantization pipelines were applied. small note — the quantization path still has a couple of model-specific knobs we need to tune, so don't flip it on for everything yet.

[00:02:10] Elena: and Product — Optimize is shipping as an opt-in beta; we have the suggestion engine that recommends batch sizes and quant profiles per route. it's intentionally conservative, we want reliability first. the UI in Console will show expected cost delta and latency delta; that was a strong ask from customer-facing teams.

[00:03:05] Ben: from sales perspective, pitch traction is good. we've closed two mid-market deals on Dedicated this month — both cited predictable latency and VPC/on-prem options as reason for switching from other vendors. pipeline is healthy but elongated for enterprise, partly because security reviews (SOC two, ISO) are taking longer.

[00:03:52] Priya: finance perspective — we ended Q4 within the plan, revenue growth is in-line, gross margins improved slightly from cost optimizations. runway still healthy but we are being conservative on hiring in H1 — we'll prioritize critical roles (core infra, security, and 2-3 customer success hires) and pause other requisitions until we finalize the Q1 budget.

[00:04:35] Lucas: reliability/ops — we ran a canary for the new kernel selection logic yesterday, small regressions in a corner-case model that uses long context; we've mitigated with fallback to older kernels. long-term fix in next sprint. also we're scheduling a full Dedicated stress test in early January with simulated burst traffic to validate autoscaling and routing fallbacks.

[00:05:20] Maya: okay that's the quick highlight reel; now a few themes and priorities for next quarter. one, product-market fit for Dedicated + Private: convert pilots to multi-quarter contracts, make onboarding smoother. two, quality and regression guardrails — we will invest in automated evals and rollback policies. three, company sizing: hiring slow, focus on leverage and automation. four, compliance — SOC2 is a must-have for many target accounts, so prioritize that.

[00:06:45] Ravi: on the technical front, the plan is to finish the quantization compatibility matrix for our top 15 models by Jan 21, and then start providing recommended config sets in Console. also we'll polish continuous batching heuristics — some customers with spiky real-time traffic prefer lower latency and we need to tune batch windows per-route.
\n[00:07:30] Elena: product OKRs for Q1: 1) reduce median cold-start latency for Dedicated by 10%, 2) ship Redwood Optimize GA with three quant profiles and per-route suggestions, 3) improve Console onboarding flow to reduce time-to-first-inference by 40%. we'll put drafts in the handbook and invite comments.

[00:08:25] Ben: sales focus Q1: convert the top 10 pilots we have into committed Dedicated deals. also increase enterprise advocacy by running two benchmark workshops per month (latency & cost comparisons) for prospects. we got feedback that customers want transparent perf numbers for specific models — we should tighten our public docs.

[00:09:10] Priya: a note on budgets — we'll carve out a small fund for targeted customer pilots (benchmarks + proof-of-concept consumption credits) but overall headcount is constrained. prioritize hires that move the needle on revenue and security/compliance.

[00:09:55] Maya: on the people side — thank you everyone for the hustle this year. we made product progress without expanding headcount too much; that was intentional. hiring will be surgical: senior infra and security first. also we need to be mindful of morale — please managers, have 1:1s before the holidays, make sure folks have clarity about Q1 expectations.

[00:10:35] Audience Q&A — submitted via Slido and live chat.

[00:10:40] Q1 (chat): "SOC two timeline?" —

[00:10:45] Lucas: we're aiming for readiness audit pack by end of Feb, audit window in March; realistic SOC two Type II in Q2 if audit timing aligns. there's lots of docs to finish — asset inventory, policy docs, evidence collection automation. some transcription note — we say 'SOC two' sometimes on calls.

[00:11:25] Q2 (chat): "What about on-prem offering?" —

[00:11:30] Elena: Private deployment on customer-managed infra is productized but onboarding flow longer. in Q1 we'll streamline the on-prem bundle and create a checklist for SEs to reduce setup time from weeks to days for typical customers.

[00:12:12] Q3 (live): "Roadmap for Redwood Optimize GA?" —

[00:12:16] Elena: GA in late Feb is our target, earliest customers by beta are giving positive feedback, but we need to harden evals and add guardrails to avoid quality regressions after quantization.

[00:12:55] Q4: "Will we increase prices?" —

[00:12:58] Priya: not planning broad price increases. we'll adjust packaging for Dedicated commits and increase premium support add-on pricing where appropriate. any price moves will be communicated well in advance.

[00:13:30] [00:13:30] Ravi: technical deep dive note — kernel selector now uses model shape heuristics and sequence length distribution; it reduces cold us, cold-start compute but needs more telemetry to auto-adjust for long-tail models.

[00:14:10] [00:14:10] Ben: sales concern — some prospects are comparing us to OpenAI's managed endpoints and Anthropic; the ask is simple: show per-model latency/cost for common workloads and provide deterministic SLAs for Dedicated. we should prioritize publishing verified benchmarks for top 5 workloads.

[00:15:00] [00:15:00] Maya: agreed. we'll commit to publishing an initial benchmark deck in January and make it available to sales and marketing. Ben, coordinate with product and eng to get representative workloads.

[00:15:30] [00:15:30] Lucas: ops note — tracing hooks for long-running requests are now in staging; they provide per-token latency breakdowns (kernel execution, kv cache hit/miss, network jitter). this should help customers debug latency spikes.

[00:16:10] [00:16:10] Elena: also adding a 'recommended profile' quickpick in Console so customers can apply Optimize suggestions without digging into all knobs.

[00:16:40] [00:16:40] Maya: two other company notes — holiday schedule: company shutdown Dec 31 to Jan 2 inclusive, small on-call rotation for infra; if you are on-call, please follow the on-call guidelines. second, board meeting debrief: we had productive conversation, board supportive of conservative hiring and focus on commercial expansion for Dedicated.

[00:17:20] [00:17:20] Priya: quick finance transparency note — we'll publish a short runway and cash position memo early next week. nothing dramatic, but we will be selective on hiring.

[00:17:45] [00:17:45] Maya: ok open mic for 20 minutes — please be brief.

[00:18:00] [00:18:00] Speaker A (Engineering): quick question on rollout strategy for quantization — will it be per-model or per-route? we saw some customers want per-route because they have mixed criticality.

[00:18:22] [00:18:22] Ravi: we'll support both. the UI will default suggestions per-route, but we'll support global and per-model overrides in the API.

[00:18:48] [00:18:48] Speaker B (Sales): follow up — can we get a short one-pager for each benchmark so sales can hand to prospects? sometimes the decks are too heavy.

[00:18:58] [00:18:58] Elena: yes, one-pagers in January, Ben and marketing will collaborate.

[00:19:20] [00:19:20] Speaker C (Support): are we changing data retention for hosted to meet privacy requests? one customer asked for 30 day retention only.

[00:19:34] [00:19:34] Lucas: we already support retention tiers in Hosted; Private/Dedicated customers can opt for zero retention. we need to make retention settings easier to configure in Console.

[00:19:50] [00:19:50] Speaker D (Research): curious about kernel selector — will the heuristics be public? customers want to understand fallbacks.

[00:20:05] [00:20:05] Ravi: we'll document the general approach and supported model classes; low-level kernel internals will remain internal but we'll provide behavior guarantees and fallback docs.

[00:20:30] [00:20:30] Maya: closing remarks — thank you everyone for the hard work. we shipped important infra and product improvements this year, landed Dedicated as a credible offering, and have a clear set of priorities for Q1: convert pilots, ship Optimize GA, finish SOC two readiness, and be surgical with hiring.

[00:21:05] [00:21:05] Maya: quick recap of next steps: we'll share roadmaps, budget memo, and SOC2 checklist early January. please take time off and come back rested.

[00:21:20] [00:21:20] Ben: quick plug — celebratory virtual (and some regional in-person) events next week, check Slack for invites.

[00:21:35] [00:21:35] Priya: thanks all, have a safe break.

[00:21:40] End of formal agenda — remaining time used for smaller breakout follow-ups and team shoutouts (not transcribed fully). Transcript may contain minor auto-caption errors and mis-attributions as typical with automated transcripts.
